text_status: the source is the submitter's own proposed specification, published for public comment on the list; it is not agreed text of any working group and a later revision can change it. The two behaviors these cases test (rejecting unsigned capability tokens, blocking dispatch when the required quorum is missing) are not defined by specification v0.1.4; they are proposed candidate tests, sourced from the pinned Rust regressions and the submitter's November 3 written input on the list (see sources and basis)
readings: an outcome is read as the record it presents: the decision and the members it carries are final, and no case asks what the implementation intended
absent_fields: an outcome lists the fields its rule reads; a field the rule reads that is missing from the outcome means the response does not carry it (an absent key is not the same as an explicit null)
field_names: outcome field names are this candidate's own representation; the source names values and rules, not a JSON binding

sources.list_record: public-agentprotocol 2026Oct/0108; the two vectors and their expected behaviors were proposed in the submitter's November 3 written input, recorded on the list at 2026Nov/0021 (independent restatement by the NTI author: an unsigned token must default to Deny, and an unmet quorum must remain Blocked) and quoted verbatim at 2026Nov/0022; the NTI author formally requested a lab run in 2026Nov/0023. https://lists.w3.org/Archives/Public/public-agentprotocol/2026Nov/0021.html ; https://lists.w3.org/Archives/Public/public-agentprotocol/2026Nov/0022.html

cases.note: the invited vector: a verifier receives a capability token with no signature and no attestation; denying fail-closed and recording an incomplete check is what the rule owes, because an unsigned token carries no attested capability
the failure mode the vector locks out: the verifier returns ALLOW for the same unsigned token, inferring a pass from an unattested token
contrast case: the token is signed and attested, so honoring it is what the rule owes; the rule is about absence of attestation, not about refusal in general
a denial that still lets the action execute is not a fail-closed denial: whatever the decision string says, an execution performed under an unattested token breaks the rule

the invited vector: quorum is set to 2 and only 1 eligible module is available; the operation must remain blocked with zero executions, because no partial execution may stand in for the quorum guarantee
the failure mode the vector locks out: the single eligible module executes once despite quorum=2, breaking the quorum guarantee
contrast case: quorum is 2 and 2 eligible modules are available, so executing is what the rule owes; the rule is about an unmet quorum, not about execution in general
with quorum unmet the operation must present the blocked state: an allow, even with zero executions, does not carry the quorum_unmet record the rule owes

reason_strings: the reason strings in these cases (unsigned_token_no_attested_capability, quorum_unmet) are candidate-defined values, chosen for this candidate's own representation. The Rust regression tests check decisions and execution counts and do not establish reason strings; check.py does not validate them
